question: How can I change the URL slug for a specific page in my Fern documentation?
ground_truth: You can change the URL slug for a specific page in Fern documentation in two ways: 1) Set the `slug` property within the `navigation` object in your docs.yml file for that page, or 2) Override the page's slug by setting it in the frontmatter of the markdown file itself using the `slug` property.

metadata.cited_context:
To modify the slug used for a page or section, you can set the `slug` within the `navigation` object. 

```yaml {{3, 6}}
navigation:
  - section: Get Started
    slug: start
    contents: 
      - page: Welcome 
        slug: intro
        path: ./docs/pages/welcome.mdx
```

In the example above, the **Welcome** page would be hosted at `plantstore.docs.buildwithfern.com/start/intro`. 

#### Override a page's slug
You can set the exact slug of a page within its frontmatter. [You can read more about the frontmatter configuration here](/learn/docs/configuration/page-level-settings#slug). 

```yaml title="docs.yml"
navigation:
  - section: Get Started
    slug: start
    contents: 
      - page: Quick Start 
        path: ./docs/pages/quick-start.mdx
```

You can set the slug in the frontmatter of `./docs/pages/quick-start.mdx` to `start-up`:

```markdown title="quick-start.mdx" {{2}}
---
slug: start-up
---
```

The page then becomes available at `plantstore.docs.buildwithfern.com/start-up`.
